in_hebrew.name: עֶסְתָּה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A name derived from the Hebrew root עסת, meaning to hide, conceal, or cover. In the Bible, the name Asta (עֶסְתָּה) appears in the Old Testament as the name of the wife of Boaz (Ruth 4:18–22) and as a name given to the daughter of Abraham and Keturah (Genesis 25:6).

in_greek.name: Αστα
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Asta in Greek is derived from the Greek word αστηρ (astēr), meaning star or constellation. In ancient Greek culture, the name Asta was sometimes given to girls born under the star sign of Aries or Taurus.

in_latin.name: Asta
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Asta in Latin has multiple meanings. It can be derived from the Latin word aster, meaning star or constellation. Alternatively, it can be derived from the Latin word anima, meaning breath or soul. In early Christian literature, the name Asta is associated with the Virgin Mary and the star of Bethlehem.
